items.title: Integrated Monitoring of Sea State: Data analysis and System Measurements
items.summary: Knowledge of the sea state is essential for safe navigation, marine operations, and offshore and coastal engineering, yet conventional measurement relies on fixed wave buoys, which are costly to deploy and provide information only at a single location. This thesis investigates the use of a ship in navigation as a sea-state sensor, estimating wave characteristics from the vessel's measured motion response through an onboard inertial navigation system (INS) integrated with GNSS antennas. The work first establishes the theoretical background on sea waves and sea-state description, including linear wave theory, wave spectra, and standard sea-state parameters, followed by the theory of ship motion in waves, covering six-degree-of-freedom dynamics, linear seakeeping, response amplitude operators (RAOs), and the effect of encounter frequency. These foundations frame the central difficulty of the problem: unlike a buoy, which is designed to follow the sea surface, a ship filters and modifies the wave excitation through its geometry, mass distribution, and forward speed, so its vertical motion cannot be taken directly as a measure of wave height. The measurement system is then validated and calibrated under controlled dry conditions, using a pendulum to reproduce buoy-like oscillations and assess the accuracy of the inertial and GNSS sensors and of the spectral processing chain developed for this work. items.title: Dem-assisted visual geolocation integrating ephemeris-based orientation correction with Multi-Scale skyline features
items.summary: Accurate geolocation in GNSS-denied mountainous environments remains a significant challenge for navigation and field operations. While vision-based methods using terrain features like skylines offer a promising passive solution, their performance is often hindered by unknown camera orientation, low feature discriminability across vast areas, and severe degradation under nighttime conditions. To address these limitations, this paper presents a novel visual geolocation framework that synergistically couples ephemeris-based orientation correction with multi-scale skyline feature matching. First, an Edge-Enhanced SegFormer-B3 (EESFormer-B3) network is developed for robust skyline extraction from query images, where a lightweight Edge Gate mechanism is integrated to refine boundary precision, particularly under low-light scenarios. Second, we propose a camera heading estimation method utilizing solar and lunar ephemeris, eliminating reliance on external heading sensors and drastically reducing the matching search space. Third, for matching, a hierarchical composite feature is designed, encoding the skyline’s global shape trends, local directional variations, and dominant structural distributions to ensure robustness against repetitive terrain patterns. Extensive experiments were conducted in a complex 700 km 2 mountainous region. The results demonstrate that our method achieves a localization success rate of 82 % (daytime) and 76 % (nighttime) within a 250-meter error threshold.

items.summary: Multisensor dataset recorded under the canopy of three orchards in southern Portugal (two orange orchards and one avocado orchard) between April and July 2026, with a purpose-built ground platform. Each session contains synchronised data from a 3D LiDAR, an IMU, an RGB-D camera and a GNSS receiver, stored as ROS 2 bags. This record is the main record of the dataset. It contains the main session, CB-11 (22 minutes, the whole of the Campinas B orchard), the calibration of the platform, a tape survey of 106 trunks that serves as a GNSS-independent reference for evaluating localization and maps, together with the LiDAR map in whose frame the trunk centres are given, and 210 images with labelled weeds and trunks (180 for training and validation and a 30-frame test set). Session CA-10 (Campinas A) is in a linked record, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23808549, and the other sessions will be released as further linked records. The README lists all eleven sessions. To protect the location of the private orchards, the GNSS fixes in the recordings were moved to a synthetic origin at latitude 0, longitude 0: their timing and relative geometry are preserved, but not the absolute position. Each session also includes the track in local East–North–Up coordinates. This dataset accompanies the MSc thesis “Mobile Robot Navigation for Vegetation Mapping in Agricultural Applications” (Instituto Superior Técnico, Universidade de Lisboa, 2026).

items.title: Reply on RC3
items.summary: Abstract. Tropical cyclone (TC) inner-core vector wind fields are essential for intensity forecasting, storm surge prediction, and structural climatology. The Cyclone Global Navigation Satellite System (CYGNSS) constellation provides dense temporal sampling and L-band precipitation-penetrating capability over the tropical belt, but its sparse, scalar wind speed retrievals have not been fully assimilated to produce kilometre-scale TC inner-core vector wind fields with global multi-basin coverage. This paper presents the QiFeng-CYGNSS dataset, which combines CYGNSS observations with a physics-guided score-based diffusion assimilation framework to reconstruct spatially complete 10 m vector wind fields from sparse scalar wind speed observations. The dataset covers 249 TCs across six active global basins during January 2020–September 2022, providing 1.5 km resolution vector wind fields at every IBTrACS reporting time with available CYGNSS coverage (4955 snapshots in total), accompanied by observation metadata and pixel-level ensemble uncertainty estimates for 138 major-hurricane snapshots. Independent validation against spaceborne C-band synthetic aperture radar, airborne Tail Doppler Radar, and GPS dropsondes indicates that the reconstructions represent TC inner-core structures at kilometre scales, reducing the absolute Vmax bias relative to ERA5 and CCMP by ~79% and ~75%, respectively, on the full sample. The dataset is freely available from Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zen

items.summary: ABSTRACT Most GPS interferometric reflectometry (GPS‐IR) studies use geodetic RHCP antennas with near‐hemispherical coverage and select the reflection zone through elevation and azimuth masks during processing. This study investigates directional GPS‐IR observations using a linearly polarized double‐ridged horn antenna (DRHA), which constrains the observation geometry at the acquisition stage. items.title: DEVELOPING A METHOD FOR DETERMINING THE DECELERATION OF ELECTRIC AND HYBRID VEHICLES DURING BRAKING
items.summary: A method for determining the deceleration of electric and hybrid vehicles during braking is proposed; its relevance is supported by post-2023 statistics (over 20 million electric cars sold worldwide in 2025; 122.7 thousand registered electric vehicles in Uzbekistan by 1 July 2026). Because braking force is shared between regenerative and friction brakes in a way that depends on battery state of charge, speed and control software, the method fuses inertial, GNSS, wheel-speed and CAN-bus data with a Kalman filter and splits the total deceleration into its regenerative and friction parts. Performance is demonstrated in a simulation study; full-scale road tests remain future work.

items.title: A Hybrid Neural-Assisted Unscented Kalman Filter for Unmanned Ground Vehicle Navigation
items.summary: Modern autonomous navigation for unmanned ground vehicles relies on different estimators to fuse inertial sensors and GNSS measurements. However, the constant noise covariance matrices often struggle to account for dynamic real-world conditions.In this work we propose a hybrid estimation framework that bridges classical state estimation foundations with modern deep learning approaches. Instead of altering the fundamental unscented Kalman filter equations, a dedicated deep neural network is developed to predict the process and measurement noise uncertainty directly from raw inertial and GNSS measurements. We present a sim2real approach, with training performed only on simulative data. In this manner, we offer perfect ground truth data and relieves the burden of extensive data recordings. To evaluate our proposed approach and examine its generalization capabilities, we employed a 160-minutes test set from three datasets each with different types of vehicles (off-road vehicle, passenger car, and mobile robot), inertial sensors, road surface, and environmental conditions. We demonstrate across the three datasets a position improvement of $12.7\%$ compared to the adaptive model-based approach. Thus, offering a scalable and a more robust solution for unmanned ground vehicles navigation tasks.

items.title: A Decoupled Variational Bayesian Adaptive Kalman Filter for MEMS INS/GNSS Integrated Navigation under Time-Varying Noise Covariances
items.summary: We evaluate a decoupled variational Bayesian adaptive Kalman filter (D-VBAKF) for MEMS INS/GNSS navigation, combining bounded fading-memory covariance matching for R with motion-regularized Bayesian model averaging over scaled Q candidates. In 50 paired trials of a 15-state, 120 s prescribed-noise simulation, 3D position RMSE reductions versus EKF-Fixed were 2.94 m (nominal paired 95% interval [1.59, 4.29] m) for 10 s outages and 7.76 m ([1.51, 14.02] m) for 30 s outages. At 60 s, intervals versus EKF-Fixed and joint-VB VBAKF included zero; all 90 s intervals included zero. In the separate no-outage simulation, Q-KL was 0.011, and the R relative error was 0.173. On one 1617 s ICM20602 drive with deterministic GNSS perturbations, full-route 3D RMSE was 27.19 m versus 30.77 m for EKF-Fixed. Across twelve repeated outage windows on that drive, the R-only variant yielded 28.19 m versus 28.86 m for the full method; BMA-Q only yielded 33.98 m versus 33.23 m for EKF-Fixed. Thus, the real-data experiment did not demonstrate an incremental accuracy benefit from adding BMA-Q to R-only adaptation, and validation on a single drive limits the generalizability of the findings. NIS coverage was 0.636 for D-VBAKF and 0.626 for EKF-Fixed, both below the nominal 0.95.

items.title: Explainable and Uncertainty-Aware Computational Geodetic Inversion: A Review and Framework for Multi-Source Earth Observation
items.summary: Geodetic inversion converts surface and remote sensing data into estimates of concealed Earth system parameters, including fault slip, magma-source geometry, subsurface mass changes, crustal strain, and time-dependent geohazard activities. This review explores geodetic inversion as a computational challenge that involves combining diverse data, optimizing and quantifying uncertainty, and providing explainable decision support. A narrative technical review was compiled using literature records from Scopus and Dimensions on topics such as geodetic inversion, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) measurements, Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR), gravity and seismic source modeling, Bayesian inversion, sparse regularization, and physics-informed learning. The literature was sorted based on the data types, inverse-problem structures, algorithmic groups, uncertainty management, and reporting standards. This review highlights five common computational layers in contemporary geodetic inversion: data harmonization, forward-model encoding, inversion and optimization, uncertainty propagation, and explainable decision support. These layers are synthesized into an explainable artificial intelligence-uncertainty quantification-computational geodetic inversion (XAI-UQ-CGI) framework for multi-source Earth observation. items.title: InSAR constraints on spatiotemporal changes in plate coupling beneath Shikoku along the Nankai subduction zone
items.summary: Abstract Estimating spatiotemporal changes in plate coupling is important for understanding the nucleation processes of megathrust earthquakes. Using Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) and Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) observations, we obtained crustal deformation around Shikoku, southwest Japan, from 2014 to 2025. We estimated slip deficit distributions along the Nankai subduction zone using kinematic fault slip inversions based on GNSS, InSAR, and GNSS-InSAR joint observations. Both the GNSS- and InSAR-based slip deficit models showed that slip deficit rates beneath central Shikoku decreased by up to 41 mm/year after 2019 relative to 2014–2018. We interpret this as a weakening of plate coupling rather than a long-term slow slip event, because the estimated slip deficit rates were not significantly negative even after 2019. Our results demonstrate that InSAR-derived velocities, which are sensitive to vertical displacements, can independently constrain broad-scale changes in plate coupling beneath inland regions, although they do not drastically improve the spatial resolution of plate coupling estimates. These findings suggest that InSAR observations provide valuable information on plate coupling changes, particularly in subduction zones where dense GNSS observations are unavailable.

items.title: Smart Farm Fence Monitoring and Intrusion Detection System with AI-Based Location Track-ing: A Review and Conceptual Architecture
items.summary: Crop damage and theft caused by wild animals, stray animals and human intruders remain a persistent problem for farmers, and a passive fence neither detects nor reports a breach. This paper presents a focused narrative review of verified studies on intrusion detection, edge artificial intelligence (AI) and location tracking for farm protection, giving priority to IEEE journal publications and supplementing them with IEEE conference and open-access sources. Four themes are examined: camera-based AI detection and deterrence; low-cost sensor-triggered and LoRa-based fog or edge systems; GNSS and LoRa-based position tracking of animals; and validation practice. The reviewed work shows that lightweight deep-learning detectors can run on low-power edge devices, that a PIR-and-camera strategy has been reported to save energy, and that signal-strength information can reduce the energy spent on continuous GPS. However, the accessible evidence is dominated by prototype-scale studies, location tracking is rarely integrated with intrusion detection, and false-alarm rate, detection latency and independent validation are seldom reported. The paper contributes a comparative table of representative studies, a proposed seven-layer conceptual architecture for a smart farm fence that combines IR/PIR sensing, camera-based AI, GPS-collar tracking and geofencing, a leakage-resistant evaluation protocol, and a prioritised list of research gaps. items.title: Geocenter sensitivity from satellite tracking
items.summary: Abstract. In this study, we revisit Kaula’s orbit perturbation theory to establish how satellite orbital geometry controls the sensitivity to degree-1 gravitational signals associated with geocenter motion along the z-axis and the (x, y )-plane, respectively. We explicitly derive the Kaula-based expressions for the degree-1 potential terms and provide complete tables of the corresponding inclination and eccentricity functions for all relevant degree-1 terms. As a case study, we apply this framework to the upcoming ESA Genesis mission, which will be the first in-orbit geodetic observatory carrying all four geodetic techniques (GNSS, SLR, DORIS and VLBI) onboard. We examine the dependence of the spacecraft orbital parameters through contributions at the spacecraft location of the degree-1 gravitational potential (V10 and V11). Our analysis shows that the V10 term associated with the geocenter’s z-component scales with sin i, implying that polar orbits maximize sensitivity to vertical geocenter variations, whereas equatorial orbits remain largely insensitive to them. Conversely, the two-term structure of the V11 expression enhances the detectability of the geocenter’s x- and y-components for equatorial or near-equatorial orbits, while retaining reduced but non-negligible sensitivity in polar configurations. items.title: Evolution of Summit Magma Pressure During the 2018 Caldera Collapse at Kīlauea Volcano
items.summary: Abstract We utilized geodetic data from the 16 May to 4 August 2018 caldera collapse sequence to refine the geometries and pressure evolution of two summit reservoirs at Kīlauea volcano: the shallower Halema‘uma‘u (HMM) and deeper South Caldera (SC) reservoirs. We modeled magma reservoirs as pressurized spheroidal cavities and constrained reservoir geometries with Global Positioning System (GPS) and Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar displacements. Inverting high‐rate GPS and borehole tilt time series recovered time‐dependent reservoir pressure changes and caldera ring fault shear stress. During the collapse sequence, the HMM reservoir accommodated episodic, co‐collapse pressure increases of 1.9 MPa (median) and a net 5.8 MPa (median) decrease. Simultaneously, the SC reservoir underwent monotonic depressurization of 6.7 MPa (median). Negligible co‐collapse pressure changes in the SC reservoir imply it was not exclusively supplying magma to the eruption vent. These results provide a coherent view of magma reservoir pressure evolution during the 2018 eruption.

items.title: Improving Smartphone Pedestrian Positioning in Urban Canyons Through PDR-Constrained GNSS Shadow Matching
items.summary: Smartphone global navigation satellite system (GNSS) positioning in building-obstructed environments is degraded by non-line-of-sight reception and multipath. Visibility-based shadow matching (SM) exploits three-dimensional building models to constrain cross-street position but has limited along-street observability. This study proposes a pedestrian dead reckoning (PDR)-constrained SM framework with two implementations: extended Kalman filter fusion (EKF-PDR/SM) using heading-orthogonal candidate search and anisotropic SM measurement uncertainty, and PDR-driven SM using candidate propagation, visibility scoring, and GNSS-proximity weighting. Evaluation used one smartphone and one pedestrian completing one traversal of each of two campus routes with different satellite-visibility conditions. Under common PDR prediction and process-noise settings, EKF-PDR/SM achieved cross-street/along-street root mean square errors (RMSEs) of 3.57/8.28 m on Route 1 and 2.46/7.83 m on Route 2, compared with 5.23/8.98 m and 4.29/12.38 m for EKF-PDR/GNSS, respectively. PDR-driven SM achieved the lowest directional RMSEs among the six compared methods: 2.92/7.47 m on Route 1 and 1.54/5.89 m on Route 2. All errors were evaluated relative to common model-derived reference trajectories. These controlled results support the use of PDR constraints to improve visibility-based SM under the tested conditions.

items.summary: This paper develops a local predictive model for geoid undulation values in the Northwestern region of Sebha, Libya, addressing the accuracy limitations of global geopotential models in regional engineering applications. items.summary: Abstract Recent developments in Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) technology have significantly improved the performance and quality of inexpensive measuring equipment, namely low-cost GNSS. These devices enable positioning with an accuracy comparable to that of geodetic-grade GNSS receivers. The main objective of this study was to verify whether such receivers are sufficient for establishing geodetic control networks using static measurement techniques, which require high accuracy in both horizontal and vertical directions. Field tests were carried out using several low-cost GNSS receivers and antennas, operated simultaneously with geodetic-grade instruments. The collected observations were processed using commercial software and compared with a benchmark campaign. The analyses considered the lengths of measurement sessions, information about antenna reference point offsets used, and the challenges in calculating baselines with low-cost GNSS receivers. items.title: Search and Rescue in Tunnels, an Integrated Approach Using Robotic Platforms
items.summary: Abstract Underground infrastructure such as road and railway tunnels requires reliable communication, localisation, and situational awareness, particularly during search and rescue operations. This article summarises developments carried out within the A‑IQ Ready project in three closely related areas: underground wireless communication modeling, survivor detection, and robotic localisation. A tunnel-specific wireless simulation platform was developed and validated against measurements acquired at the underground facility Zentrum am Berg, enabling realistic prediction of quality-of-service metrics and supporting AI-based communication assessment. Demonstrations at Zentrum am Berg confirmed the suitability of the developed technologies for search and rescue applications in complex underground infrastructure. items.title: Trust-driven adaptive weighting for robust GNSS state Estimation under interference condition
items.summary: Reliable state estimation in Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) becomes challenging when measurement statistics are distorted by signal interference. Jamming, spoofing, multipath propagation, and environmental disturbances may significantly increase residual variance and introduce biases in pseudorange observations, which leads to degradation of navigation accuracy and loss of estimation reliability. Conventional robustness mechanisms typically rely on threshold-based fault detection, residual monitoring, or classical robust estimators. Although such approaches mitigate large outliers, they often employ binary measurement exclusion or purely statistical reweighting and therefore do not explicitly account for the reliability of individual measurement channels. This paper proposes a trust-driven adaptive weighting framework for GNSS state estimation under interference conditions. The method introduces a dynamic trust coefficient assigned to each measurement channel based on statistical quality assessment and risk-aware evaluation of its potential impact on the navigation solution. Residual variance is used to quantify measurement stability, while a channel risk factor incorporates geometric sensitivity and anomaly likelihood. The resulting trust coefficients regulate measurement influence through adaptive modification of the measurement covariance matrix within the Extended Kalman Filter.

GNSS station position time series contain stochastic variations, often referred to as noise, that exhibit spatial correlations over distances of thousands of kilometers. The impact of these spatial correlations on the uncertainty of longterm station velocity estimates, however, remains poorly modeled and is therefore largely neglected. To address this limitation, we build on recent advances in the characterization and modeling of the spatio-temporal correlations of the noise in GNSS station position time series. We develop a multi-scale spatio-temporal noise correlation model and use it to derive the full covariance matrix of errors in a global station velocity field. Our results show that the spatio-temporally correlated noise induces significant and non-trivial correlations across station velocity errors, which depend not only on the distance between stations but also on the temporal overlap of the station position time series. items.title: Hard Sample Mining for GNSS Spoofing Detector via Physics-Based Meta-Learning Optimization
items.summary: GNSS spoofing detectors flag spoofing signals through sensing features such as carrier-to-noise density ratio and signal quality monitoring statistics. Training stronger detectors—and mapping detector performance boundaries—requires hard traction samples that systematically challenge those features, yet such samples are expensive to obtain under closed-loop replay and vary with the traction target. We propose Physics-Based Meta-Learning Optimization (PBMO) as a hard sample miner: it archives traction trajectories across traction targets, warm-starts a new traction target with Offline-RGPE and physics-based priors, and refines candidates with Physics-prior Guided Pattern Search (PhGPS). Hardness is scored by a conformal upper bound on the fraction of moving-variance windows that exceed channel thresholds. On a four-channel moving-variance (MV) detector, comparisons show that PBMO lowers the mean conformal upper bound by 30.7% relative to an unoptimized frequency-difference-lock strategy, and under the same online search budget remains below cold-start, nearest-neighbor, and mean-trajectory initializations. A USRP X310 wired loopback at one traction frequency preserves this ordering.

items.title: Topology-Consistent Trajectory Event Matching for GNSS-Denied Vehicle Initial Localization
items.summary: Vehicle initial localization under global navigation satellite system (GNSS)-denied conditions remains challenging because an odometry trajectory provides relative motion but no absolute road-network reference. Inspired by the coordinated use of self-motion information, recognizable route cues, and route continuity in biological navigation, this paper proposes a topology-consistent trajectory-event matching method. The method organizes odometry into ordered trajectory structure pairs formed by adjacent normal turning events and their intervening corridors, while a standard road-network map is automatically enhanced with internal direction-change points to construct corresponding map-side structures. Local candidates are retrieved according to direction, length, turning, and corridor-morphology consistency, and successive candidates are jointly confirmed under topological continuity. The confirmed discrete correspondence is then refined by local trajectory-image matching to estimate the continuous starting position. Experiments on KITTI-360 sequences 00, 08, and 09 with 135 starting positions yield an overall initialization success rate of 88.9%; successful trials achieve a mean error of 2.46 m and a median error of 2.29 m. The results show consistent performance across the evaluated road scenarios while indicating that sparse turning events and locally ambiguous road structures remain important limiting conditions.

Abstract

Tropospheric ZTD estimates agreed with geodetic equipment to 3–8 mm RMS, and PWV retrievals agreed with radiosonde and reanalysis products to within 1–3 mm. items.title: RANSAC-based iterative data refining method for multiple outliers in GNSS positioning
items.summary:
Abstract 
                   Effectively dealing with multiple outliers is indispensable for achieving reliable navigation and positioning performance in GNSS. The iterative data snooping (IDS) method is commonly used to identify outliers in a forward stepwise manner. Nevertheless, its effectiveness is often compromised by masking and swamping when multiple outliers are present. Recently, the iterative data refining (IDR) method was proposed as a backward alternative to IDS, which identifies potential inliers from the initial outlying set. However, its performance depends critically on the preset maximum number of suspected outliers (qmax), as this critically affects the quality of the initial outlying set. A large qmax covers all outliers at the expense of estimation accuracy, whereas a small qmax may fail to mitigate the masking and swamping effects. To address this dilemma, a dynamic adjustment strategy for qmax is adopted. Meanwhile, random sample consensus (RANSAC) is employed to evaluate whether the resulting inliers obtained by IDR still contain outliers, which guides the adjustment of qmax. Therefore, this paper proposes a RANSAC-based IDR method that dynamically adjusts qmax in a piecewise increasing manner. items.title: Detection-Aware Delayed Multi-Sensor Fusion for UAV GNSS Spoofing Mitigation: A Factor-Graph-Based Framework
items.summary: GNSS spoofing can progressively corrupt unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) navigation when manipulated position solutions are fused before integrity assessment. Existing detection methods often use dead-reckoning references such as visual–inertial odometry (VIO) without fully accounting for accumulated drift or GNSS-dependent global alignment. This paper presents a closed-loop software-in-the-loop (SITL) evaluation platform and a detection-aware delayed multi-sensor fusion framework for UAV GNSS spoofing mitigation. The platform couples state estimation, flight control, vehicle dynamics, and sensor feedback to enable Monte Carlo evaluation under realistic navigation–control interactions. A cumulative sum (CUSUM) detector monitors consistency between GNSS and drift-compensated VIO, while recent GNSS factors are quarantined and incorporated into a factor graph only after integrity screening. Experiments quantify false-alarm rate, detection probability, and latency across detector settings and spoofing deviation rates. Onboard implementation and controlled injection experiments further assess real-time feasibility and hardware transferability. Under the evaluated sensor conditions and gradual-drift attack model, a 10–15 s window yielded detection probabilities exceeding 96% for attacks with a deviation rate of 0.5 m/s, with an approximately 3% false-alarm rate. These findings demonstrate the framework’s potential for spoofing mitigation and the platform’s utility for closed-loop eval

items.summary: Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals are the primary source of positioning, navigation and timing information in civil aviation. The open structure of civil GPS signals makes them inherently vulnerable to spoofing, and reported incidents affecting commercial aircraft have increased sharply since September 2023. Existing countermeasures either detect spoofing without restoring the navigation solution, depend on dedicated antenna arrays, or require offline training data, so none of them simultaneously satisfies the operational constraints of a standard single-antenna airborne receiver. This paper proposes a hardware-free, real-time framework that combines received signal power analysis with an Anchor Selection Method (ASM) and Weighted Geometric Dilution of Precision (WGDOP). The remaining authentic satellites are then enumerated exhaustively, and the subset that minimises WGDOP is adopted as the optimal anchor set for a linear least-squares position solution. items.title: STM32-Based Landmine Detection and GPS Localization Robotic Vehicle
items.summary: Autonomouslandmine detection remains a majorsafety challenge, as conventional manual methods expose personnel to hazardous environments, take considerable time, and may offer limited spatial tracking of detected threats. These limitations are particularly significant in military, humanitarian demining, and hazardous-terrain operations where accurate localization, autonomous navigation, and real-time monitoring are required. This thesis presents an Autonomous GNSS-Guided Mine Detection and Geofenced Monitoring Robot designed to autonomously survey a defined area and identify and spatially record potential metallic mine locations. The system provides dedicated access for field operators and administrators, where operators monitor robot movement, detected targets, and surveyed regions while administrators manage operational data, geofencing, and monitoring functions. The core mechanism combines GNSS positioning with centimeter-level correction, geofencing, barometric sensing, metal detection, and motor control to continuously calculate robot position and constrain movement within the predefined boundary, providing transparent rule-based navigation rather than relying on a black-box navigation model. Supporting features include autonomous movement, virtual fencing, boundary violation prevention, metal-detection marking, real-time position tracking, sensor-status monitoring, location logging, historical data visualization, and remote dashboard monitoring.

items.title: Neural Terrain Classification and Fuzzy Adaptive Covariance Tuning for Improved Outdoor Mobile Robot Localization
items.summary: Abstract Accurate and reliable localization is essential for autonomous outdoor mobile robots operating with low-cost sensors under varying terrain conditions. In such environments, the performance of an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) strongly depends on the appropriate selection of process- and measurement-noise covariance matrices, while fixed covariance parameters often fail to represent terrain-dependent uncertainty. The terrain-specific covariance parameters obtained offline using PSO are incorporated into a Mamdani-type fuzzy inference system, which adapts the EKF covariance matrices online according to the estimated terrain type and its associated class-dependent reliability coefficient. The framework was experimentally validated on a wheeled mobile robot using commanded velocity inputs, low-cost Global Positioning System (GPS) measurements, and Real-Time Kinematic Global Navigation Satellite System (RTK-GNSS) reference trajectories collected over multiple outdoor terrain types. Compared with a baseline EKF using fixed covariance matrices, the proposed adaptive approach reduced the average root mean square error by 9.7% and the mean absolute error by 10.2%, with the largest improvements observed on deformable terrains. The results demonstrate that terrain-aware covariance adaptation provides an effective strategy for improving outdoor localization performance using low-cost sensing systems.

items.title: Onboard-navigation-aided federated fusion for telemetry tracking of high-dynamic flight-test targets
items.summary: Accurate guidance information is essential for telemetry antennas to maintain stable target tracking during flight tests. When the onboard navigation solution degrades or ground-based external tracking measurements are interrupted or abnormal, antenna pointing errors may increase and the telemetry link may become unstable. To improve the reliability of telemetry tracking, this paper applies adaptive federated filtering to a telemetry fusion tracking problem based on onboard navigation and ground-based external measurements. The downlinked SINS/GNSS integrated navigation solution is used as the reference solution at the ground station, and a reference-error state model is established. Ground-based radar measurements and optical measurements are then used to estimate and correct the position and velocity errors of the reference solution. The corrected target state is further converted into azimuth and elevation guidance angles for the telemetry antenna. In the adaptive fusion process, innovation-based fading factors and information allocation coefficients are used to adjust the reliability of different measurement branches and reduce the influence of abnormal measurements. Simulation results under representative disturbance scenarios verify the feasibility of the proposed method and indicate that the corrected target state can provide a more stable guidance reference for telemetry antenna tracking.

items.title: Rapid earthquake magnitude estimation from fuzzy C-means clustering-weighted fusion of seismogeodetic PGD and PGV
items.summary: Rapid and reliable earthquake magnitude estimation is essential for earthquake early warning and tsunami-impact assessment, particularly for large events for which conventional seismic estimates may saturate. This study develops a seismogeodetic magnitude-estimation framework that combines peak ground displacement (PGD) and peak ground velocity (PGV) derived from near-colocated GNSS and strong-motion observations. Fuzzy C-means clustering is used to construct observation-dependent prior weights, while robust and geometry-aware weighting are introduced to reduce the effects of anomalous observations and uneven station distributions. The method was evaluated using 1,147 paired observations from 19 earthquakes with moment magnitudes ranging from 6.1 to 9.0. In leave-one-earthquake-out validation, the PGD-only and PGV-only solutions yield mean absolute errors of 0.338 and 0.320 Mw, respectively, whereas joint PGD/PGV estimation reduces the error to 0.261 Mw. The full robust geometry-aware solution yields an MAE of 0.259 Mw. A two-event holdout test gives a fused mean absolute error of 0.194 Mw, although fusion does not outperform the better single-parameter estimate for every event. These results demonstrate that combining PGD and PGV provides the main improvement in magnitude estimation, while robust and geometry-aware weighting offer additional event-dependent benefits.

items.title: AGGO: Concept and realization of a geodetic observatory in South-America
items.summary: Geodetic observatories form the backbone of global geodetic reference frames. This article reviews the definition of the global geodetic reference system in terms of its origin, orientation, and scale, and its realization through reference frames. At geodetic observatories, reference points are materialized by instruments and survey markers. To achieve the highest possible accuracy, complementary measurement techniques are employed, often operating near the limits of what is technically feasible. Accordingly, a geodetic observatory brings together complex instruments, including a radio telescope for very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), a satellite laser ranging (SLR) system, receiving stations for global navigation satellite systems (GNSS), atomic clocks, absolute and superconducting gravimeters, and complementary sensors. The spatial relationships between the reference points of these instruments are determined through precise local surveys (local ties). The current instrumentation of the Argentine-German Geodetic Observatory (AGGO) is described as an example of the range of measurement techniques needed to establish and maintain a reference site within the global geodetic reference frame. Measurement data collected at AGGO are made freely available through international services.
